articles.title: ‘It’s about to go global’: American college football rocks into Wembley – a photo essay
articles.summary: Our photographer, Tom Jenkins, captures the colour and razzmatazz as college football arrived in the capital, hot on the heels of successful NFL outings in recent years. Rarely has Wembley Way seen or heard such a commotion.
body: Pundits from Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff Show were broadcasting live from outside the venue – a curious spectacle in which the hosts even ate fish and chips in front of a fake Grenadier guard – as thousands of supporters around them waved placards and chanted college anthems. It fuelled a tailgate party atmosphere that wouldn’t have felt out of place in the States.

Dubbed the Union Jack Classic, the game pitted two sports-mad colleges, Kansas and Arizona State, against each other in front of 46,000 partisan fans, with many of the players one day hoping to play in the NFL.

“There’s a lot more grit and hunger in college football than in the NFL,” said Trey Latham, an ambitious 22-year-old linebacker for Kansas, on the eve of the clash. “College football teams go at it neck and neck. NFL players know they’re already fed, but we’re trying to feed our loved ones. There are scouts watching and people are desperate [to make it].”

The only previous college football game to be staged in the UK was in 1988, when Richmond beat Boston University at Crystal Palace. And while 42 NFL games have been staged in the UK capital over the past 19 years, college football has remained absent.

articles.title: ‘I needed an IV’: shoes melt as turf temperature reaches 157F in Eagles-Titans game
articles.summary: Eagles coach says game was ‘hot as shit’ Cam Jurgens had to replace cleats several times. The Tennessee Titans were happy to get off the field on Sunday, and not just because they lost their second game in a row.
body: Amid sweltering conditions in Nashville, the temperature on the artificial turf at Nissan Stadium reached 157F (69.4C), according to the Fox broadcast.

“It was hot as shit, everybody was as hot as shit,” Philadelphia Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said after his team’s 24-20 win. “I didn’t play a snap and I had to get an IV. I … appreciate how much the players fought through because it wasn’t easy.”

Nashville was under a heat warning for Sunday’s game, which kicked off at noon local time. The air temperature was 95F (35C) with a heat index of 105F (40.5C). However, inside the bowl of the stadium the surface of the artificial turf was much hotter.
Eagles offensive lineman Jordan Mailata said the temperatures were another reason for the players union to push for a ban on artificial turf.

articles.title: How many times has a player scored a hat-trick in a Premier League loss?
articles.summary: Sunderland's Brian Brobbey scored the first hat-trick by a player on a losing side in the Premier League for 19 years - but how many others have done so?
body: Brian Brobbey etched his name in Premier League history on Sunday after scoring a hat-trick as part of the losing side.
The Netherlands striker is now only the fifth different player to do so in a Premier League match, after netting three times during Sunderland 's 5-3 defeat by Manchester City.
It is the first time that has happened in the top flight since 2007, and only the sixth time since the Premier League's formation in 1992.
The last player to achieve the feat was Roque Santa Cruz, scoring a hat-trick for Blackburn Rovers in a 5-3 defeat by Wigan Athletic in December 2007.

articles.title: Thirteen-year-old swim sensation sets women’s 200m butterfly record at Asian Games
articles.summary: Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi wins the first major title of her young career – but says her performance was ‘only so-so’ The 13-year-old Chinese swimmer Yu Zidi set an Asian Games record as she scorched to gold on Sunday’s first full day of competition.
body: The schoolgirl, who turns 14 next month, took the women’s 200m butterfly crown in a Games-record 2min 05.08sec.
It was the first major title of her young career, less than two years out from the Los Angeles Olympics.
“It was only so-so,” a smiling Yu said after receiving her medal.
Yu became the youngest medallist in swimming world championships history last year when she took home relay bronze aged 12.

articles.title: NRL open investigation into fans after top referee pelted with rubbish at Eden Park
articles.summary: Ashley Klein targeted after Warriors’ season ended by Knights. Official had to be protected by security on way off pitch in Auckland. The NRL has threatened to ban fans who peppered referee Ashley Klein with projectiles, with the integrity unit investigating the aftermath of the Eden Park clash.
body: Vision from after full-time in Newcastle’s 12-10 win over the Warriors on Sunday showed Klein being hit with a raft of bottles, cups and rubbish as he walked from the field.
The footage shows Klein having to be protected by security, as fans abused the veteran referee and projectiles rained down on him.
The NRL immediately launched an investigation into potential breaches of their spectators’ code of conduct. An Integrity Unit investigator had been at the ground.
“If found guilty, they will be banned for a period of time from attending NRL games,” ARL Commission chairman Peter V’landys told AAP.

articles.summary: Northern Ireland's return to Uefa Nations League B will see them face a player manager Michael O'Neill calls "one of the best in the world" but they enter the campaign without their own captain.
body: The build-up to Northern Ireland's 2026 Nations League campaign has been dominated by the future of Ceadach O'Neill and the always thorny issue of eligibility.

With the Arsenal forward included in Michael O'Neill's 28-man squad for this four-game window, the 18-year-old appears set to add to his two senior caps across the next two weeks, likely ruling out any future switch of international allegiance despite an approach from the Republic of Ireland.
While one prominent storyline seems as if it will soon be put to bed, there is plenty more to look out for as Northern Ireland make their return to League B.
For the first time since June 2022, Northern Ireland will face four games in the same international window.

articles.title: Pistons' Michael Blackstone has cancer, but it's not end of his story
articles.summary: For Pistons' Michael Blackstone, a stage 4 lung cancer diagnosis started with pain in his right shoulder. He wants people to learn from his situation.
body: For Michael Blackstone, a cancer diagnosis started with a seemingly benign pain in his right shoulder.

The Detroit Pistons’ executive vice president of basketball operations since 2024, Blackstone was an assistant general manager with the New Orleans Pelicans when the pain began during the 2023 offseason. The team medical staff worked on it for several weeks, believing it to be an out-of-place rib.

It got worse after Las Vegas Summer League, though, prompting Blackstone to meet with his primary care physician in Florida. She ordered an x-ray, which led to a CT scan, which led to a PET scan and, finally, a biopsy that confirmed the reason behind his discomfort.

Blackstone, who is 54 and a lifelong nonsmoker, was diagnosed with stage 4 lung cancer. It had already metastasized to his spine, hence the pain. Since July 2023, he has been in treatment at the Mayo Clinic in Jacksonville, Florida.

articles.title: Tommy Carr gets first Michigan football moment: 'We believe in Tommy'
articles.summary: "He's a student of the game," Michigan football coach Kyle Whittingham said. "He's a football junkie, and to me, his ceiling is exceptionally high."
body: The camera panned to the suites in Michigan Stadium and he was hard to see behind Tammi Carr jumping for joy and sharing a long hug.

But there he was – former Michigan football coach Lloyd Carr, in his familiar blue hat with a maize Block "M," smiling from ear to ear. His grandson, U-M backup QB Tommy Carr, had just thrown the first touchdown of his college career − a high-arching, perfectly placed ball on a slot-fade from 19 yards out to highly regarded freshman Salesi Moa (in the first score of his career, too).

It was an emotional moment for the Carr family, who went through heartbreak with the loss of Tommy's younger brother, Chad, to diffuse intrinsic pontine glioma – a brain cancer better known as DIPG – in November 2015. On Saturday, Sept. 19, however, there was pure joy. That was true in Ann Arbor, as Tommy had his first Michigan moment, and in South Bend, Indiana, where oldest brother CJ led No. 3 Notre Dame to a 27-10 win over Michigan State.
